Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a large, well-defined soft tissue mass in the right upper and mid-lung zones (right paratracheal/mediastinal region) that is causing significant deviation of the trachea to the left. This mass effect explains the retrosternal chest pain and the observed tracheal displacement, distinguishing it from collapse (which would pull the trachea toward the lesion) or simple lymphadenopathy without a discrete large mass.
